author: human
request:
Feature request: the vet list answers "which specialties does this vet hold",
but staff also ask the inverse — "which vets hold this specialty". Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; managing
  veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before (non-goal NG-2
  is unchanged).
- The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link
  from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come
  as a follow-up request.

Add a specialty directory page:

- GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored
  name, each with the veterinarians holding it.
- Each veterinarian is shown by full name: first name, then last name (for
  example "Helen Leary").
- A veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty; the page
  lists specialties, not the full vet roster.
- All specialties render on one page — no pagination.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can see which veterinarians hold each specialty
summary: A read-only specialty directory lists every specialty the clinic knows under its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it, all on one page. It is reachable by its address alone.
acceptance_criteria: Every specialty the clinic knows is listed under its stored name, together on one page, with no pagination.
Each veterinarian holding a specialty is shown under it by first name then last name, for example "Helen Leary".
A veterinarian holding no specialty does not appear on the page.
A specialty no veterinarian holds is still listed, with no veterinarian shown under it.
The specialties, and the veterinarians under each, are presented in a stable order rather than an arbitrary one.
When the clinic knows no specialty, the page opens with nothing listed rather than failing.
No navigation entry and no link from any other page leads to the page; it is reached by its own address, which the owner stated as GET /specialties.html.
The page carries the navigation every page carries (REQ-SYS-001), and any wording on it is presented in the reader's language like every other page (REQ-LANG-002).
non_goals: managing veterinarians or specialties through the application (NG-2 stands, unchanged)
a navigation entry or a link from another page to the specialty directory
a search, filter, or query input on the page (NG-9 stands: only owners are searchable)
changing the existing veterinarian directory (REQ-VET-001) or its paging
notes: Grounded in the intake-decision at line 1. Boundary check: the page is read-only, so NG-2 is untouched; it carries no query surface, so NG-9 is untouched; REQ-SYS-001 requires each page to carry navigation, not to be reachable from it, so the no-link decision does not contradict it. No Non-Goals row changes, so no scope_overrides. Narrowest readings taken where the request was silent, each recorded as an Open Question in docs/prd.md: ordering is only required to be stable; a specialty held by no veterinarian is listed with nothing under it and is not marked in words; no visible entry point (the owner named one as a possible follow-up request). The address GET /specialties.html is the owner's stated wording, kept out of docs/prd.md as mechanism. No prd-autofix records to audit.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The specialty directory is the existing vet feature-package shape applied to the inverse relationship: a Spring Data lookup repository, a thin controller, and a Thymeleaf template under templates/vets/. Every piece instances an in-force pattern, so the design delta is one adjustment, not new ground. The adjustment: the page needs every specialty the clinic knows, including one no veterinarian holds, and Vet owns the only mapping of the holding relationship. Specialty carries no inverse side, so the vets package gains its first lookup repository (SpecialtyRepository, modelled on owner/PetTypeRepository which returns its lookup values name-ordered) and the directory is assembled in memory from two independent reads rather than by adding a bidirectional mapping. Basis for the covering claims: direct reads of Vet.java (Set<Specialty> is the owning @ManyToMany, EAGER, no mappedBy inverse on Specialty.java), VetRepository.java (cached findAll()), VetController.java, PetTypeRepository.java, and templates/fragments/layout.html. No IDE oracle is connected in this run, so no search_symbol citation backs them; file reads are the basis, which is stronger than grep but weaker than symbol resolution. docs/system-design.md now carries three new Contracts rows and REQ-VET-003 on Vet, Specialty, and VetRepository.
integration_points: SpecialtyController is a new package-private @Controller in the vet package serving GET /specialties.html; it fetches specialties from SpecialtyRepository and veterinarians from VetRepository.findAll(), hands both to SpecialtyDirectory, and selects the view. It takes no request parameter.

SpecialtyDirectory is an immutable value object: it pairs each specialty with the veterinarians holding it, orders specialties by name and veterinarians by last name then first name, and keeps a specialty no veterinarian holds with an empty collection. It is unit-testable without Spring.

SpecialtyRepository returns every specialty in name order, following the explicit-@Query shape of owner/PetTypeRepository. A specialty is reachable independently of any veterinarian, which the paged VetRepository read cannot deliver.

The template is templates/vets/specialtyList.html, replacing fragments/layout with a menu selector that matches no existing menuItem, so the page carries navigation (REQ-SYS-001) without gaining an entry of its own.
No new message key is needed: the existing keys specialties, name, and vets cover the heading and both column headers. No new cache is declared; CacheConfiguration is untouched.

patterns.description: lookup-value repository returning every row in name order via an explicit @Query — the model for SpecialtyRepository
thin @Controller reading a repository, populating the model, returning a view name — the model for SpecialtyController, minus the pagination helpers
feature template replacing fragments/layout with a menu selector; th:each table body over the model attribute
Value object row: SpecialtyDirectory is immutable, equal by value, and holds the derivation the controller must not

risks.risk: Adding an inverse @ManyToMany(mappedBy) to Specialty to reach its veterinarians. With Vet's association EAGER and spring.jpa.open-in-view disabled, the inverse side would have to be eager too, producing a mutual eager fetch and changing the persisted mapping for both entities.
risks.mitigation: Do not touch the mapping. Read specialties and veterinarians separately and pair them in SpecialtyDirectory (architecture-principles.md § Domain Core: aggregates reference each other by identity; § Persistence and boundary mapping).

risks.risk: Putting the grouping, ordering, and empty-specialty handling in the controller body. architecture-principles.md § Pattern Catalog states a new rule added to a controller is a fresh violation, not covered by the recorded deviation.
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyDirectory owns the derivation and is tested without a Spring context; SpecialtyController only fetches, delegates, and selects the view (architecture-principles.md § Design Validation Checklist, Web controller row).

risks.risk: Stale directory: veterinarians arrive through VetRepository.findAll(), which is @Cacheable("vets") with no eviction configured — system-design.md § Open Questions from the Survey, item 5.
risks.mitigation: Reuse that read rather than adding a second cached path; declare no new cache. The staleness surface is the existing one, unchanged.

risks.risk: A new user-facing message key would have to land in all eleven bundles or I18nPropertiesSyncTest fails, and REQ-LANG-002 forbids hard-coded page text.
risks.mitigation: Use the existing keys specialties, name, and vets. If wording genuinely needs a new key, add it to every messages_*.properties in the same change (docs/prd.md REQ-LANG-002).

risks.risk: Adding a navigation entry or a link to the new page, which the slice's non_goals exclude.
risks.mitigation: Do not edit fragments/layout.html. Pass an unmatched menu selector so the active-tab comparison simply never matches.

risks.risk: A new endpoint widens the exposed surface (security-principles.md § Realization, 'Widening the exposed surface').
risks.mitigation: The route is GET-only, read-only, takes no parameter, and publishes specialty and veterinarian names already public on /vets.html. No new trust boundary; rendering relies on Thymeleaf's default escaping, which stays on (system-design.md § Threat Model, cross-site scripting row).

notes: Verdict is minor, not covered: three new contracts are added and docs/system-design.md changed, but every one instances an existing in-force pattern, so no ADR is warranted (architecture-principles.md § Pattern Catalog: an in-force pattern is adopted without one). Deviation from the prd-entry's file_targets, deliberate: the slice gets its own SpecialtyController and SpecialtyControllerTests rather than extending VetController, because the naming rule prefixes a controller by the domain noun it serves and VetController would otherwise carry a second repository dependency and a second unrelated surface. The prd-entry's five test names carry over unchanged to SpecialtyControllerTests; SpecialtyDirectoryTests covers the ordering and empty-specialty derivation without a Spring context. Naming: 'specialty directory' is the confirmed term in docs/ubiquitous-language.md; the entry type inside SpecialtyDirectory takes a domain noun with no prohibited suffix. Effort rated routine: each file has an adjacent seam demonstrating its shape. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the handoff log, so the autofix audit is empty. The prd-entry's open question about a visible entry point stays open and out of scope.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Supply-chain NVD status, so a human or CI closes it: no OWASP Dependency-Check plugin is configured in build.gradle, and this reviewer has no network access, so no NVD match ran in this review — the dependency set is 'not verified against the NVD', not clean. Resolved framework versions read from build.gradle: Spring Boot 4.1.1, io.spring.dependency-management 1.1.7, GraalVM buildtools 1.1.2, CycloneDX 3.4.1.

Unbounded-read note (informational, no attacker path): showSpecialtyDirectory reads every specialty and every veterinarian per request with no page limit, and SpecialtyRepository carries no @Cacheable while VetRepository.findAll() does. Both collections are clinic-sized lookup data and the PRD requires one unpaged page, so the response size is bounded by seeded data an attacker cannot grow through any route in this change — no unbounded-allocation finding. Worth revisiting only if specialties ever become writable (NG-2 currently forbids it).
approved_aspects: No injection surface into data access: SpecialtyRepository.findSpecialties() is a fixed JPQL string literal with no parameters and no request-derived value; ORDER BY is a constant column reference (security-principles Injection row).

Output escaping preserved: specialtyList.html renders every request-reachable value through th:text (specialty name, vet first/last name). No th:utext, no th:attr injection, no inline JavaScript, and no Thymeleaf preprocessing (__${...}__) on any value; grep over the changed template surface found preprocessing only in the pre-existing vetList.html pagination links, untouched by this change. Escaping matches the neighboring vetList.html implementation of the same concern (Pattern Consistency).

No mass-assignment surface: SpecialtyController takes no @ModelAttribute, no @RequestParam, and no @PathVariable — the handler's only argument is Model, so there is no request-bound type and no missing setDisallowedFields (security-principles Mass assignment row is not engaged).

Exposed-surface widening is bounded and read-only: the one new route GET /specialties.html is a GET with no input, and the data it publishes (specialty names, vet names) is already published by the pre-existing /vets.html and /vets routes. No management endpoint, no mutating route, no broadening of actuator exposure — not weaker than the baseline in system-design.md Security Context.
No path traversal or resource resolution from input: the view name is the private static final constant VIEW_SPECIALTY_LIST; no request-derived value composes a filesystem, classpath, or view path.

No secrets introduced: the diff adds no credential, token, key, or connection string; the changed files contain no logging at all, so no secret or user value reaches a log line (no log-injection surface either).

Concurrency safety of the new singleton: SpecialtyController holds only two repository references and no mutable state; SpecialtyDirectory is constructed per request and is deeply immutable — both records defensively copy through List.copyOf in their compact constructors, and the two comparators are stateless static finals.
No deserialization, serialization, reflection, shell execution, file I/O, XML parsing, regex, or java.util.Random in the change (grep over the new vet-package sources and templates).

No supply-chain delta: build.gradle, settings.gradle, and gradle/ are unchanged in the change set, so no new dependency and no repository or TLS configuration change to clear the four checks in system-design.md Adding a New Dependency.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: findSpecialties()'s hand-written JPQL (`SELECT specialty FROM Specialty specialty ORDER BY specialty.name`) is never executed against a real datastore in any test. SpecialtyControllerTests mocks SpecialtyRepository via @MockitoBean, and SpecialtyDirectoryTests never touches the repository. The design's own model, PetTypeRepository.findPetTypes(), gets real-database coverage in ClinicServiceTests (a Spring-Boot-Test-backed suite over the real H2 fixture); SpecialtyRepository has no analogous test. A typo in the query string, a wrong ORDER BY column, or a mapping mismatch would ship undetected — the mocking policy's 'Real I/O for integration' requirement is unmet for this new query.

theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldEqualAnotherBuiltFromTheSameReads constructs `new SpecialtyDirectory(listings)` directly, bypassing the suite's own createASpecialty/createAVeterinarian factory convention. testing-principles.md 'Test Data Construction > Factory Methods' requires production types to be constructed through a test-owned factory, not the raw constructor.
findings.fix: Add a small factory (e.g. createADirectoryFrom(listings)) or route through SpecialtyDirectory.of(...) consistently, and use it here instead of calling the record constructor directly.

findings.description: theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldCarryTheSiteNavigationWithoutAnEntryOfItsOwn only checks the specialty page's own rendered output. It does not cover the other half of the prd.md acceptance criterion and coverage-map Done-when bullet 4 -- 'no navigation entry and no link from any other page leads to the page' -- since no test asserts an existing page (e.g. vets/vetList.html or the fragments/layout.html nav) omits a link to /specialties.html. Nothing currently links to it because layout.html was left untouched, but that fact has no regression guard.
findings.fix: Add an assertion (e.g. in VetControllerTests, or a template-level check) that the existing vets list / nav fragment output does not contain 'specialties.html', guarding against a future edit accidentally adding the link.
